From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Alicia Hart <alicia.hart@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood evaluation - DPA & SCC question

Hi Alicia - great talking earlier, and really appreciate the clear list. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

1) SOC 2: Redwood completed a SOC 2 Type II audit covering our hosted API and control plane services; most recent report: 2025-11-10. I'll attach the SOC 2 summary and provide the full attestation under NDA if needed.

2) DPA: Attached is a draft Redwood DPA (Redwood_DPA_draft_v1.pdf). Our standard position is that AcmeHealth will be the Controller and Redwood the Processor. The DPA includes processor obligations, subprocessors, data deletion/return terms, and incident notification timelines.

3) SCC Module: For controller -> processor relationships the recommended EU SCC path is Module 2 (Controller to Processor). I've attached an SCC matrix (SCC_module_matrix.xlsx) that maps typical vendor roles to modules.

4) Vendor questionnaire: Thanks for the file - we'll start populating it. Marissa (security/legal) and Neha (privacy) will kick off internal responses and aim to return a completed copy within 3 business days.

Proposed timeline: 
- Today: Share DPA draft + SCC guidance (attached) - done.
- By Fri 2026-02-13: Completed vendor questionnaire and SOC 2 summary.
- Early next week: Legal review on your side; propose a short call with AcmeHealth Legal/InfoSec if there are redlines.

Next steps for you: please confirm if Module 2 is acceptable for AcmeHealth (you may want to confirm with Oliver/InfoSec). If Acme wants us to sign a modified DPA, we can take redlines and circulate a mark-up for review. We can also route the DPA via DocuSign (link to follow).

I'll follow up with the completed questionnaire and SOC summary by Friday.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Phone: (415) 555-0126

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_draft_v1.pdf; SCC_module_matrix.xlsx

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 11:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood evaluation - DPA & SCC question

Rishi - quick notes from Legal/Security review of the draft DPA and SCC recommendation: 

- Module: confirm Module 2 (Controller -> Processor) is appropriate. That matches our standard DPA flow. If Acme insists on Module 1 we should flag that as it implies controller->controller which is atypical for a hosted inference provider.
- Data categories: we should confirm whether Acme will send any special category personal data (e.g., healthcare PHI). If so, we need to add HIPAA-specific controls and potentially a BA agreement scope.
- Subprocessors: keep the current subprocessor list, but offer a 30-day notice for additions (standard).
- Incident timelines: our current SLA is 72 hours initial notification for confirmed incidents; Legal suggests keeping that and providing weekly updates until resolution.

I can prepare a redline set for the DPA and a short comment doc for Acme's Legal. Also we'll take the vendor questionnaire - aiming to return it by EOD Fri (2026-02-13).

Marissa Cole
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

--
Internal action: Marissa will prepare DPA redlines; Neha will confirm PHI scope with Acme when they return the questionnaire.
